  • Method Details

    • applySlimyEye

      public static net.minecraft.world.InteractionResult applySlimyEye(net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack stack, net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Player player, net.minecraft.world.entity.Entity target)
      The Slimy Eye apply verb on either side: a target whose verdict is EyeItemService.Verdict.CAN_HAVE gains eyes carrying the stack's appearance on a freshly rolled placement variant, consuming one eye. Any other target passes (PASS), so its own use (riding, trading, a chest) still happens; another player mayAffect(Player, Entity) protects refuses (FAIL). The client answers from the same verdict, so its SUCCESS predicts exactly the server's application. The mob and boat paths (interact(Player, Level, InteractionHand, Entity)) and the sneak self-apply (SlimyEyeItem#use) route through here. Vanilla records no item use for any of them, so this does.

    • interact

      public static net.minecraft.world.InteractionResult interact(net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Player player, net.minecraft.world.level.Level level, net.minecraft.world.InteractionHand hand, net.minecraft.world.entity.Entity target)
      Route supported entities through normal loader interaction hooks. Eligible application and harvesting are predicted on the client, so success also consumes the target's own use, and on Fabric the click's second interact packet: that packet's callback would otherwise find a just-harvested mob eyeless and let vanilla shear it. Irrelevant actions pass through to vanilla. Spectators pass here and at the other use entry points because the loaders' use hooks can fire before vanilla's spectator test.

    • markHeadDrop

      public static void markHeadDrop(net.minecraft.world.entity.LivingEntity mob, net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack stack)
      Give a head item an eyed mob drops in its death loot the mob's whole eye state, when the head is the mob's own kind (SkullEyeState.entityFor(Block)) and carries no eyes yet, so the placed head shows the mob's arrangement and colors. Players are left out: their death drops are their inventory. Each loader routes every stack of the death-loot phase here; any other stack is left alone.

    • onDeath

      public static void onDeath(net.minecraft.world.entity.LivingEntity mob, net.minecraft.world.damagesource.DamageSource source, Consumer<net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack> dropSink)
      Attempt the shears-on-kill harvest, routing the resulting eye through each loader's death-loot phase: NeoForge and Forge add it to the LivingDropsEvent collection, Fabric spawns it from a dropAllDeathLoot mixin at the same point. Neither depends on mob_drops, so the rule is checked here.

    • selfRemoveWithShears

      public static net.minecraft.world.InteractionResult selfRemoveWithShears(net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Player player, net.minecraft.world.InteractionHand hand)
      Sneak + right-click air with shears to shear your own eyes off — the self-serve counterpart to another player having applied a Slimy Eye to you. One Googly Eye drops carrying your effective appearance and the shears lose one durability. Optometrist shears do it cleanly; plain shears additionally deal a bare-handed hit's worth (base attack damage, whatever the main hand holds) of ModContent.SELF_SHEAR damage, which has no attacker so PvP and team rules don't cancel it. Returns InteractionResult.PASS when it doesn't apply (spectating, not sneaking, not shears, no eyes, googlyEyesEnabled off) so the vanilla item use proceeds.

    • useOnSkull

      public static net.minecraft.world.InteractionResult useOnSkull(net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Player player, net.minecraft.world.level.Level level, net.minecraft.world.InteractionHand hand, net.minecraft.world.phys.BlockHitResult hit)
      Right-click-on-block entry point for both eye items aimed at a placed mob head: a Slimy Eye on a head whose verdict is EyeItemService.Verdict.CAN_HAVE goes to applySlimyEye(ItemStack, ServerPlayer, BlockEntity, Direction), Optometrist shears on an eyed head, with eyes enabled, to harvestSkull(ServerPlayer, InteractionHand, BlockEntity, Direction). Both sides decide those cases from the state they hold, and the client answers InteractionResult.SUCCESS in exactly them, so it neither runs nor sends the item's own use on top (a sneaking player's self-apply or self-shear). Anything else, including plain shears, an eyed head, or a spectator's click, returns InteractionResult.PASS. The Slimy Eye comes here rather than through Item#useOn for the reason a mob's click does: a modded head block can have a use of its own that takes the click first.
